extracted.intended_audience: congressional staff, regulators, journalists, VW stakeholders (dealers, customers), and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript of a congressional oversight hearing focused on Volkswagen's emissions defeat device: expectations for corporate remedies, dealer/customer communications, regulatory cooperation, investigations, and compensation. Contains statements and questions that articulate standards the Committee expects VW to meet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix vehicles to achieve emissions standards
rubrics_metrics.description: 'We know that we can fix these vehicles to achieve emission standards.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixes must come from Technical Engineering Department and be coordinated with actions in Europe and the U.S.; technical remedies (Generations 1–3) should be developed and shared with agencies; VW should be able to demonstrate that post-repair vehicles meet regulatory NOx limits and provide supporting data to EPA/CARB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve fuel economy and engine performance or compensate customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee concern that fixes might 'substantially change the cars' and that owners who relied on fuel economy/performance should be compensated if fixes degrade those attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VW's current understanding is customers 'will get the MPG on the Monroney label'; any 'significant differences' in performance or fuel economy must be disclosed to agencies and discussed as part of compensation; VW should quantify expected MPG/performance impacts and offer remedies/compensation where performance is materially reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate environmental and public-health impacts of excess NOx pollution
rubrics_metrics.description: Members asked: 'How do you plan to mitigate the harm caused by this excess pollution emitted into the air over the last seven years?' noting emissions 'up to 40 times the allowable limit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VW must engage in discussions with regulators on remediation of environmental/health harms, consider studies cited by EPA, and present mitigation proposals as part of remedy scenarios; acknowledgement of scope (relative contribution percentages) is not a substitute for mitigation planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide immediate and ongoing financial support to dealers
rubrics_metrics.description: VW described measures: paid maximum bonuses, removed customer satisfaction targets, provided a discretionary fund wired to dealers, free flooring/floor plan, and increased incentives for loyal customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support should be significant enough to aid dealer cashflow/profitability; explain amounts, eligibility, and distribution; use district managers and Sales Operations Managers to explain discretionary funds; maintain transparency about what payments are dealer-directed vs customer-directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform and guide dealers and call centers with timely, accurate information
rubrics_metrics.description: VW said it 'set up frequently-asked questions' and is 'guiding the dealers with real-time the same information we have,' providing letters, videos, and calls to National Dealer Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications must specify which models are affected, how existing and on-lot vehicles will be handled, and customer-contact guidance; ensure call centers and dealer staffs receive synchronized messaging; document communications timeline and materials provided (letters, videos, FAQs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct thorough investigations and identify responsible individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee expectation that VW 'examine its compliance processes' and that investigations (managed by Jones Day) find 'who did what, when, how, and why'; references to suspensions of personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent counsel to investigate, report on findings, identify responsible parties where permissible, and take appropriate disciplinary or legal action; be clear about investigative scope, limitations (e.g., German law on naming), and milestones for delivering results to stakeholders and regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen compliance processes to prevent recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Volkswagen will examine its compliance processes and standards and adopt measures to make certain that something like this cannot happen again.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present specific process and organizational changes, timelines for implementation, and accountability structures; streamline processes, adopt new controls, and communicate how these reforms will be enforced across global operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear timelines and resource estimates for remedies and recalls
rubrics_metrics.description: VW described Generations of software fixes, plans to give software to agencies (January, mid-year), and estimated that repairing ~430,000 cars could take '1 or 2 years minimum' with '5 to 10 hours' per repair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share detailed timetable for software delivery, agency review, parts availability, and phased repair rollout; estimate per-vehicle labor/time and overall program duration; update timelines as technical complexity warrants and notify regulators and dealers of changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and disclose compensation approaches including buybacks or repairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Members asked whether VW would 'buy back the inventory' and about losses in vehicle value; VW stated 'Our plan is to fix the cars' but said customers would be compensated if fixes cause differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate options (repairs vs buybacks), quantify loss-in-value scenarios, publish criteria for customer compensation, and decide whether dealer inventory buybacks are appropriate; communicate chosen approach and rationale to regulators and affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate fully with regulators (EPA, CARB) and provide test data/software
rubrics_metrics.description: References to sharing test results with EPA/CARB, proposing recalibration fixes, and the need to discuss timing and technical details with agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share software, test data, and calibration details with relevant agencies for independent verification; participate in laboratory and on-road testing as requested; do not withhold material information and be responsive to agency inquiries and test results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize safety, quality, and integrity over profitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee expectation voiced: 'I would hope that safety, quality, integrity are top priorities, and profitability comes along there as a part of that picture.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate responses and remedial actions should center on customer safety and product integrity; internal metrics and dealer incentives should be adjusted to reflect compliance and safety priorities rather than sales/profit-only targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurately quantify scope of affected vehicles and be transparent about numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about whether the defeat device is found in 'nearly 500,000 vehicles' and whether VW is 'confident in that number.' VW: 'We are very confident in this number.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence and methodology for affected-vehicle counts, admit uncertainty where present, update numbers as investigations proceed, and avoid understating or overstating scope to stakeholders and regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect dealer and employee livelihoods by addressing cashflow and job certainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee asked when employees and dealers will 'have some certainty as it relates to the jobs' and VW stated dealer profitability is a top objective and that programs address cashflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design relief programs aimed at preserving dealer operations and employee jobs (discretionary funds, incentives, flooring support); disclose eligibility, duration, and monitoring of such programs; include plans to support affected employees where necessary.
